related_questions.question: Are home COVID tests still accurate?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, home COVID tests are still considered accurate, particularly when used correctly and when symptoms are present. While they may be less sensitive than laboratory-based PCR tests, especially for detecting early or asymptomatic infections, positive results from at-home antigen tests are generally reliable. To increase accuracy, especially with negative results, repeat testing is often recommended.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, home COVID tests are still considered accurate, particularly when used correctly and when symptoms are present

list.title: Accuracy of Positive Results:
list.snippet: At-home antigen tests are generally good at detecting the virus when someone is actively infected and symptomatic.

list.title: Accuracy of Negative Results:
list.snippet: At-home tests may not always detect the virus in the early stages of infection or in asymptomatic individuals.

list.title: Importance of Repeat Testing:
list.snippet: Because of this, the FDA recommends repeat testing after a negative result, especially if symptoms are present or there has been potential exposure.

list.title: Symptoms Matter:
list.snippet: At-home tests are generally more effective when used by individuals experiencing symptoms, according to Harvard Health.

list.title: Test Type:
list.snippet: It's important to remember that antigen tests are less accurate than PCR tests.
